name: Osteoradionecrosis of the Mandible

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and radiological findings

criteria.description: Exposed necrotic bone in the mandible persisting for more than 3 months after radiation therapy
History of radiation therapy to the head and neck region
Radiological evidence of bone destruction, sequestration, or osteolysis in the mandible
Exclusion of tumor recurrence or osteomyelitis as cause of bone necrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of exposed necrotic mandibular bone persisting >3 months post-radiation with radiological evidence and history of radiation therapy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging; biopsy may be required to exclude malignancy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-healing intraoral mucosal ulceration overlying mandible

common.symptomName: Mandibular pain localized to affected area

common.notes: May indicate secondary infection or inflammation

common.symptomName: Trismus due to fibrosis and inflammation
searchTerms: difficulty opening mouth from tight muscles

common.symptomName: Fistula formation between oral cavity and skin
common.notes: Cutaneous fistula may develop in advanced cases
searchTerms: abnormal connection between mouth and skin
opening draining from mouth to outside skin

occasional.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness of the lower lip and chin (mental nerve neuropathy)
searchTerms: numbness or tingling in lower lip and chin
loss of sensation in chin area

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection with purulent discharge

searchTerms: foul mouth odor related to necrosis

occasional.symptomName: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) due to pain or trismus
searchTerms: pain or tightness causing swallowing problems
trouble eating due to mouth stiffness

rare.notes: Severe infection with fever and malaise
searchTerms: bone infection with fever and malaise

rare.notes: Chronic skin opening draining necrotic material
searchTerms: chronic draining hole between skin and mouth
long-term drainage from mouth to skin

laboratory: Normal or elevated inflammatory markers if secondary infection present
Microbiological cultures from necrotic bone or fistula discharge may identify secondary pathogens
imaging: Panoramic radiograph showing radiolucent areas of bone destruction and sequestra
CT scan demonstrating cortical bone erosion, sequestration, and pathological fractures
MRI may show marrow edema and soft tissue involvement
other: Clinical history of prior head and neck radiation therapy
Physical exam revealing exposed necrotic bone

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of active infection with systemic signs
Lack of prior radiation therapy history
More rapid progression and response to antibiotics
Radiological evidence of soft tissue mass
Absence of exposed necrotic bone without tumor
History of bisphosphonate or antiresorptive therapy
Similar clinical presentation but no radiation history

redFlags: Rapidly progressive swelling with airway compromise
Signs of systemic sepsis or osteomyelitis
references: Marx RE. Osteoradionecrosis: a new concept of its pathophysiology. J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 1983 May;41(5):283-8.
Rao SD, et al. Osteoradionecrosis of the mandible: a review of pathophysiology and management. Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol. 2018;125(3):e1-e10.
